newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers mostly lower on NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers mostly lower on NYMEX.

text.p: North American bunker prices mostly fell in brisk trade on Thursday, following NYMEX crude oil and heating oil futures downward, players said.
NYMEX December crude oil futures fell on news that rival Kurdish factions agreed to extend a cease-fire in northern Iraq.
The news renewed hopes that a long delayed U.N. oil-for-food deal for Iraq would be implemented.
"The market came way off after crude oil starting falling," said one East Coast trader.
December crude ended 93 cents down at $23.35 a barrel.
In the East Coast, New York Harbor spot 380 CST fell $9, trading between $117 and $118. 180 CST fell $8 to 122/123 amid a frenzy of buyers trying to catch good numbers after months of high values.
In the Gulf Coast, Houston spot 380 CST fell $7 to $112/113 and 180 CST dropped $5 to 116/117, players said.
The West Coast saw a slight uptick due to firm demand and tight supply.
Seattle 380 CST edged up $1 to $118/119 and 180 CST was also valued $1 higher at $120/121, traders said.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
